So many days, I find myself pondering human nature. There are so many people out there that constantly and consistently prey on others. We had to invent locks for humans to secure themselves and their possessions from other humans who would happily victimize them. Is this the truth of our nature? Humans have put their intellect toward creating things with which to victimize others. Weapons, torture devices, all the way up to high-tech ways to steal from others with identity theft, card skimmers, you name it. Some take delight in the misery of others. Why are people like this?

It causes me deep sorrow to think about it. The thought of causing harm to another is anathema to me.
Why do we as a race do evil?

I simply blame the way we evolved, still having a lot of competitive traits that allowed our great ancestors to pass their genes down. I'm not too informed on evolution theory, but having traits of cooperation and social interaction is what set our kind from most others (I say most because a lot of other animals have these, too). Knowing this, I have hope that, eventually, the human race will evolve these traits out and we can then become a peaceful race.

So, my answer to your question is: "because we haven't evolved those genes out yet."

Who is your favorite character from the series?

Jaime. He's got a great storyline. He's a good fighter but a crappy knight until he loses his hand. Then he becomes a crappy fighter but a good knight. The lesson in humility, and seeing him work through that, is really interesting. He's pretty misunderstood by everyone. He's called the Kingslayer, but no one bothers to listen to his side; it was a perfectly reasonable action to take when the King was planning to burn down an entire city. Once I understood his motivation, I feel like that decision was more honorable than some of the stuff Ned did, at least when you look at the fall out. And Jaime's v Ned's definition of right and wrong is very interesting too. Great illustration of how sometimes the ends justify the means.
Jaime became so awesome once he lost his hand. Before that he was a massive douche.

And also there are so many awesome characters.

First off, i just found this verse and it's awesome. Now let's get down to business. What are we considering sandwiches? I see in the sidebar that hotdogs aren't considered sandwiches, but in a previous post in this sub someone mentioned a spring roll recipe and there wasn't an issue. I understand that we are trying to be a friendly verse, but what do we consider sandwiches?
What are we considering a sandwich?

Hi wheresbigfoot. Glad you like the sub!

A sandwich is anything that has filling or sandwiched between two or more pieces of bread. Spring rolls technically wouldn't be allowed, because they are rolled up inside of one piece of bread (or whatever that is). Hot dogs are enveloped inside of one bun, making them not sandwiches.

Things that are not sandwiches also include: Pitas, tacos, burritos, quesadillas, pizza, and "open faces sandwiches" (seriously. Just put another piece of bread on there).

Of course, you're allowed to talk about whatever you want in the comments, but submissions should be sandwiches only, which is why the spring roll wasn't an issue. Now, if he had tried to submit the spring roll, it would have broken the rules. He also said that it would taste just as good when sandwiched.

But as you said, this verse is a friendly verse, so when in doubt, go ahead and post it! Chances are, it's going to be fine. I might seem like a sandwich snob, but I promise I'm not. :D

I appreciate the reply. I would disagree with you that pitas are not sandwiches, but I can respect your opinion and authority on the matter. Apart from that though, I am totally fine with the qualifications.
